Date: Nov 20, 2026
Location:
Incheon, South Korea (ICN), KR
Company:
Green Climate Fund
Background:

The Green Climate Fund is the world’s largest dedicated multilateral climate fund, serving as the climate finance partner of choice for developing countries. We invest in impactful, innovative and catalytic programmes and projects that deliver practical climate solutions where they are needed most.

As GCF marks a decade of climate action, its achievements demonstrate a sustained commitment to global climate finance. Since approving its first project in Peru’s Amazon basin in November 2015, GCF has grown to a portfolio exceeding USD 19 billion, comprising more than 330 projects across over 130 developing countries. This experience informs an ambitious transformation agenda to make climate finance more responsive to country needs, faster to access and more impactful at scale.

GCF aims to become at least a USD 50 billion fund by 2030. Its transformation is rooted in impact and efficiency, improved access, a focus on the most vulnerable, and mobilization of public and private financial flows for climate action. GCF’s scale, risk appetite and flexibility enable it to convene partners and stakeholders in innovative arrangements for greater impact.

The Fund seeks to engage a Regional Presence Project Management Support Consultant to join its team at headquarters in Songdo, Republic of Korea, for a period of twelve (12) months. The assignment will support project mobilization and sustained implementation; integrated planning and scheduling; the establishment and administration of governance and project control arrangements; the development and maintenance of common readiness frameworks and location checklists; active implementation support for priority workstreams and locations; and the progressive transition of established processes and records to steady-state owners.
Objective and expected outcome

The objective of the consultancy is to provide senior-level strategic and project management leadership for a twelve-month period of Regional Presence implementation. The Consultant will shape and take ownership of the integrated delivery strategy and approach, engaging across departments and at all levels to drive progress against an agreed plan, anticipate and resolve dependencies, manage risks and issues, and give workstream owners and GCF management a reliable, forward-looking view of activities, deadlines, decisions, costs and readiness. The Consultant will advance priority workstreams and locations from mobilization through implementation, operational launch where applicable, stabilization and planned transition to steady-state ownership. By the end of the assignment, GCF should have a robust, well-governed delivery framework, embedded planning, tracking and reporting tools, documented lessons learned, and a clear handover and transition package to sustain implementation and operations.
Role

GCF is establishing Regional Presence through offices in Panama City, Amman, Nairobi, Abidjan and Suva. This enterprise-wide initiative will introduce a geographically distributed operating model and requires coordinated implementation across governance, Host Country Agreements, organizational design, workforce mobility, finance, procurement, facilities, information technology, safety and security, risk and controls, business continuity, communications and change management. Implementation will be phased from preparatory work and host country negotiations through office establishment, staff deployment, commencement of operations, stabilization and transition to steady-state ownership.

The Consultant will report to the Manager of General Services, in their capacity as the GCF Regional Presence Programme Manager, hereafter referred to as the Programme Manager, and will act as the senior project management lead and principal delivery adviser, with delegated responsibility for day-to-day delivery under their overall oversight. The Consultant will operate with a high degree of autonomy and may be asked to deputize for the Programme Manager on project delivery matters and, when authorized, to represent the Regional Presence delivery function in senior management fora. The Consultant will design, establish and run the programme management and control arrangements; plan and sequence work with workstream owners; constructively challenge strategic assumptions, timelines and interdependencies; and drive follow-through on agreed actions. During the twelve-month assignment, the Consultant will lead programme mobilization and sustained implementation, set the cadence for planning and review cycles, and proactively provide analysis, options and recommendations on progress, dependencies, risks, decisions, costs and readiness across the five locations and relevant GCF functions. The Consultant will also lead the progressive handover of established processes and records to designated owners.

The assignment is intended to support a twelve-month implementation period but is not expected to complete every element of the full Regional Presence lifecycle, which may extend beyond the consultancy. The Consultant will have no authority to approve readiness, accept risk, authorize deployment, commit GCF, approve expenditure or assume responsibilities assigned to GCF management or functional owners, but is expected to exercise senior-level, independent professional judgement, make clear recommendations and escalate decisions in a timely manner. The assignment requires a full-time onsite presence at GCF Headquarters in Songdo, with authorized travel to Regional Presence locations if required.
Duties and responsibilities
The Consultant will provide the following services, together with closely related support reasonably required for the assignment:

Provide strategic leadership and direction for Regional Presence implementation, advising the GCF Programme Manager and senior management on delivery strategy, phasing and sequencing options, trade-offs and priorities across the five locations.

Lead the development, maintenance and continuous improvement of the Regional Presence Master Implementation Plan and integrated schedule, working with workstream owners to define scope, sequencing, milestones, critical path and resource needs.

Establish, lead and run the programme management office (PMO) function for Regional Presence, including standards, templates, tools, cadence and controls, using GCF-designated systems (including Asana where applicable) and avoiding parallel systems of record unless authorized by the GCF Programme Manager.

Provide functional direction and guidance to any PMO support staff, analysts or consultants assigned to Regional Presence, setting work priorities and quality standards, and coach GCF staff and focal points in sound programme management practice.

Drive delivery of agreed activities, milestones and deliverables by holding owners to account for deadlines and dependencies, resolving bottlenecks, and escalating material or persistently overdue actions to the GCF Programme Manager with proposed solutions.

Maintain end-to-end oversight of critical activities across Host Country Agreements, premises, procurement, technology, finance, workforce mobility, safety and security, communications and operational launch, identifying cross-workstream dependencies and gaps early.

Engage and influence senior management, workstream leads and location focal points at all levels, clarify ownership, reconcile conflicting priorities and deadlines, and build alignment on plans and next steps.

Design and lead the governance framework and facilitate senior-level governance meetings, including agendas, decision papers, presentation materials, minutes, action records and follow-up, so that decisions are well prepared and taken in a timely manner.

Lead risk, issue, dependency, assumption, decision and change-control management: facilitate identification and assessment with responsible GCF owners, propose mitigation options and track resolution.

Design and manage the decision-gate and readiness framework, ensuring that required actions, owners, due dates, supporting evidence, functional sign-off and status are recorded consistently and that gates are prepared in time for decision.

Develop and apply standardized location readiness checklists covering legal, premises, security, healthcare, information technology, business continuity, operational controls, banking and local support requirements.

Compile and challenge readiness inputs submitted by designated technical owners, identify gaps and unresolved dependencies and drive their closure. The Consultant will not assess technical adequacy or certify compliance; relevant functional owners will validate and sign off their requirements.

Track and drive host-country and location milestones, including Host Country Agreement milestones, host country actions, missions, premises and service-establishment milestones, and anticipate risks to launch dates.

Consolidate and analyze implementation cost, commitment, forecast and resource information provided by Finance and other responsible functions, highlight variances, trends and decisions required, and advise on implications for budget, scope and schedule.

Oversee the production of the programme dashboard and status reports showing progress, upcoming milestones, overdue actions, key risks and matters requiring management attention, with clear analysis and recommendations.

Prepare and present briefing materials, presentations and options papers to the GCF Programme Manager, senior management and governance bodies, translating complex information into clear, decision-oriented messages.

Oversee programme files and version control and set the standard for quality of programmeinformation; promptly challenge gaps or inconsistencies in source information, noting that workstream leads and functional owners remain responsible for its accuracy, completeness and timely submission.
Key deliverables and indicative timing

Mobilization package — initial twelve-month workplan, delivery strategy, programme management approach and governance framework, stakeholder map and contact list, baseline delivery calendar and programme-file structure, within two weeks of commencement.

Integrated plan and PMO package — Master Implementation Plan, integrated schedule and critical path, milestone calendar, responsibility matrix, PMO standards and templates and action tracker, with initial versions within four weeks and active management throughout the assignment.

Risk, dependency and readiness management package — risk, issue, dependency, assumption and decision registers with mitigation recommendations, decision-gate and readiness framework, location readiness checklists and an evidence index, with initial versions within eight weeks and active management throughout the assignment.

Monthly reporting and governance package — dashboard, analytical status report with recommendations, meeting records, decision and action summaries, and briefing materials for management, produced each month or in accordance with the agreed governance calendar.

Quarterly implementation review — consolidated review of progress against the master plan, critical-path milestones, resource and cost information, key risks and dependencies, readiness status, and recommended priorities and corrective actions for the following quarter, submitted and presented to senior management at the end of each quarter.

Mid-term review and forward plan — assessment of the first six months of implementation, including achievements, outstanding gaps, lessons learned, recommended adjustments to approach and a refreshed workplan and schedule for the remaining assignment period, submitted and presented to senior management by the end of month six.

Final handover and transition package — current editable programme files, status of all milestones and registers, outstanding-action summary, ownership and transition matrix, lessons-learned report and recommendations for continued implementation or steady-state management, submitted before completion of the assignment.
Authority and decision rights

The Consultant will provide senior-level leadership of programme management and recommend courses of action, but will not make technical, contractual, financial, personnel, security or procurement decisions; commit GCF to any course of action; approve expenditure; certify readiness; or represent GCF without prior authorization. The Consultant is expected to prepare well-reasoned, strategic options and recommendations for decision by senior management. All technical conclusions, sign-offs and approvals remain with designated GCF officials.
Performance management

Performance will be assessed throughout the assignment, including through periodic reviews aligned with the agreed workplan and deliverables. Assessment will be based on the quality and timeliness of delivery against the integrated plan; effectiveness of the governance, PMO and control arrangements established; proactive identification and resolution of risks, dependencies and blockers; quality of strategic analysis, advice, reporting and recommendations to senior management; effective senior-level leadership, influence and collaboration with the GCF Programme Manager, workstream owners and focal points; and the quality of knowledge transfer, handover and transition.
Essential qualifications and experience
An advanced university degree (Master’s or equivalent) in business administration, management, public administration, engineering or a related field.
A recognized programme or project management qualification (e.g., PMP, PgMP, PRINCE2 Practitioner, MSP).

Fifteen (15) or more years of progressive professional experience in project or programme management, management consulting, PMO leadership or transformation delivery, including at least five (5) years in a senior management or leadership role leading complex, multi-stakeholder, enterprise-wide initiatives.

Demonstrated experience establishing and leading PMO functions and teams, and designing and running project and programme governance and control frameworks, including integrated plans, critical-path management, risk and issue management, benefits and cost tracking, and management reporting.

Strong analytical, structuring and problem-solving skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information into clear recommendations and executive-level advice and presentations; advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word and PowerPoint.
Experience with Asana, SharePoint, Microsoft Teams or comparable collaborative project-management platforms, including setting up tools and standards for others to use.
Proven ability to advise, influence and align senior executives and cross-functional teams without direct authority, and to drive accountability and resolve conflicts.
Excellent organization, judgement, communication and follow-through, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams independently and to escalate effectively.
Desirable qualifications and experience
A recognized change management qualification (e.g., Prosci, APMG Change Management, or equivalent).
Senior-level experience with an international organization, development institution, management consultancy or geographically distributed, multi-site project.
Experience in organizational design, office establishment, operating-model transformation or similar change initiatives.
Working knowledge of French, Spanish or Arabic.
Application Process
The closing date for applications is 04 December 2026, 23:59 (KST). Applications submitted after the closing date may not be considered.
Interested candidates are invited to submit their CV and a cover letter detailing their qualifications and experience relevant to the role.
Candidates of all nationalities are welcome to apply. Please indicate your earliest availability to take up the assignment and notice-period required, if employed.
In case of any technical issues, please email: procurement@gcfund.org.
Note: Due to the high volume of applications, only candidates shortlisted for interview will be contacted regarding the status of their application.
